finding.claim: deleteAccount ignores the result of canDelete, so any caller can delete any account by id (broken access control / IDOR).
finding.source: id (path parameter, per route comment line 19) and User u supplied by the caller; authentication of u is not in this repository

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) receives attacker-chosen id and caller-supplied u
canDelete(u, a) evaluated but its boolean result is discarded; no throw or return

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) has correct logic but is unused here; assertCanDelete (13-17) is not called in deleteAccount; closeAccount (27-31) enforces the check on line 29, so the omission is a defect; no other guards in the method. Reachability from an HTTP route and authentication of User are unverified.

verdict.guard_found: Only canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) is present, and it is called as a bare statement at line 22 with its boolean discarded. assertCanDelete (13-17) is defined but never called in deleteAccount. No other control sits between the caller and accounts.remove(id) at line 23. "none" effective.
verdict.reason: deleteAccount at AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) as a bare statement with its result discarded, then unconditionally calls accounts.remove(id) at line 23, while closeAccount at line 29 correctly uses assertCanDelete, so any caller that reaches this method can delete any account. The one caveat is that the HTTP route and the authentication that produces the User are not in this repository, so "any caller" depends on that external layer, but nothing in the repo blocks it.
